summary.headline: Shriram Properties posted record Q1 FY27 sales of INR484 crores (+10% YoY) but revenue of INR271 crores (+4%) and PAT of INR11 crores lag, with growth back-ended.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 sales value rose 10% YoY to INR484 crores on 0.85 million sq ft, the company's highest-ever Q1, driven by launches at Shriram Stellar (Chennai), Shriram Southbrook (Kolkata) and Green Meadows phase (Chennai). Revenue of INR271 crores, EBITDA of INR42 crores and PAT of INR11 crores were steady, with margins diluted by low-margin legacy Kolkata handovers. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance, pointing to Q2 and H2 OCs (about 2,900 units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential) and a back-ended launch calendar. Net debt to equity stood at 0.29x, with gearing expected to rise in FY27.

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Shriram Stellar, a premium launch late June, sold about 20% on launch weekend; Green Meadows new phase (0.2 million sq ft) also launched.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Shriram Southbrook (0.4 million sq ft) launched; branded plotted development had about 55% of inventory sold within 30 days. Legacy Grand One and Sunshine One handovers carry thin margins.

segments.name: Bengaluru / Pune
segments.commentary: Doddagubbi JDA (about 0.7 million sq ft saleable) added in Q1, expected on board end-Q3/early Q4; Manjari (Pune, 2.3 million sq ft via FSI purchase) expected to launch after plan approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: sales value INR3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth) and collections INR2,100-2,200 crores (26-30% growth), per Q&A.
Revenue recognition expected to grow at least 20% in FY27; PAT growth guided at 20-25%; FY27 PBT margin about 8-9%.
FY28 mission reiterated: sales value about INR5,000 crores, revenue INR2,500 crores, PBT about INR250 crores (around 10% margin); FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

Handover pipeline: 410+ units of pent-up handovers, 2 projects (400+ units, INR160 crores) for OC in Q2, and 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores) for H2; total 2,900+ units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential for balance of FY27.
Management expects gearing to rise temporarily in FY27, with long-term comfort at 0.5x-1.0x net debt to equity.
Management reiterated FY27 sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores; launch GDV of about INR6,000 crores from 7.23 million sq ft targeted supply.
capex_capacity: FY27 launch calendar: about 6 million sq ft planned out of 7 million sq ft potential across Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata; 2 projects (0.7 million sq ft) launched in Q1.

Current pipeline 33.7 million sq ft (16 million ongoing, 17.7 million upcoming) with GDV potential about INR13,530 crores; 7.3 million sq ft (GDV above INR6,000 crores) at advanced stage for addition in 3-6 months.
Kolkata: about 110 acres of land; 2.3 million sq ft apartment approval obtained pre-election, to be released in phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft, with only one phase possible in FY27.
Management targets nearly doubling the upcoming pipeline over 18-24 months.
Cash flow: INR88 crores invested in new projects in Q1.
demand_pricing: Sustenance sales prices rising about 4-5% annually, versus 10-15% in the post-COVID period; launch prices set by competition in each micro-market.
Average mid-market selling price about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft, versus about INR5,000 pre-COVID; Sunshine 2 and 3 realising about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft.
Management sees no material slowdown in conversion or housing loan application momentum; Bengaluru launches described as slow, upper-end investment demand flagged as softer.
Legacy Shankari (Chennai) and Grand One (Kolkata) realise about INR4,500-5,000 and INR18-24 lakh tickets, dragging margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 mission (INR5,000 crores sales, INR2,500 crores revenue, INR250 crores PBT) still intact and how credible is a 10% PBT margin versus historic EBITDA of 7-8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the targets. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (FY23), 22.6% (FY24), 18.4% (FY25) and about 13.5% (FY26), with PBT of 8.8%, 7.7%, 9% and about 5.3%. It guided FY28 EBITDA margin of 22-24% and PBT around 10%, based on project-level build-up and not land sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is sales value growing 40-50% while collections grow only 26-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections follow project progress: 10% on booking, 20% after agreement, then construction-linked. Launches are back-ended to Q3-Q4, so collections ramp in later quarters and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of FY27 launch GDV versus sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores look right; the balance comes from new launches off about 7.23 million sq ft supply worth about INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata land plan and value?
qa_highlights.answer: About 104-106 acres approved for apartments, villas and plots, with a 3-year build and 5-year handover target. Management estimates INR6.5-7.5 crores net contribution per acre and INR1,200-1,400 crores free cash over about five years; bulk sale at INR3.5-4 crores per acre was rejected as uneconomic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 PBT margin 10% and what drives the margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PBT margin guided at 8-9%. Margins are product-mix driven: Grand One, Shankari and Sunshine One handovers are low-margin, with Sunshine 2 and 3 and post-2019 launches expected to restore mid-20s EBITDA margin and 9-10% PBT, mainly in H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will tax write-backs boost PAT in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax write-backs cannot be predicted; they arise only from loss-making subsidiaries recognising deferred tax assets. PAT growth guided at 20-25% without a write-back assumption.

risks_watch: Margin delivery: FY26 EBITDA margin fell to about 13.5% and PBT to about 5.3%; FY27 PBT guided at 8-9% and FY28 PBT ~INR250 crores (~10%) depends on product mix shift to post-2019 launches, which management said may not show until H2 FY27 and FY28.

Revenue timing: Q2 OCs cover 2 projects (400+ units, INR160 crores) and H2 covers 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores); any slippage in OC timing would push the INR1,560 crores handover potential and the 20%+ revenue growth.

Back-ended sales and collections: FY27 sales INR3,300-3,500 crores and collections INR2,100-2,200 crores rely on Q3-Q4 launches (Manjari pending Pune plan approval, T-John pending plan sanction), so approval delays would hit both.
Balance sheet: gearing expected to rise temporarily in FY27 (net debt to equity 0.29x today, long-term comfort 0.5x-1.0x); debt cost about 11%.

Kolkata monetisation: 2.3 million sq ft apartment approval to be released in phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft, with only one phase possibly in FY27; land plan economics (INR6.5-7.5 crores per acre net contribution) are management estimates; bulk sale rejected.
Demand: Bengaluru launches slow and upper-end investment demand softer; management sees no material conversion slowdown, but watch launch absorption in Bengaluru and Pune.
key_quotes: Yes, the numbers are right. And Kolkata land sale is not a significant part of it.
We are looking at PBT stabilizing in the range of about 10% margin.
So, this year, we might be in the 8% to 9%.

Tax write-back is difficult to predict because tax write-back happen only when there is a project where we are having a loss that is being recognized, there's a deferred asset getting created only then the tax write-back happens in the joint venture
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on the full-year FY27 guidance and the FY28 mission, backed by handover visibility and the launch calendar, but cautious on timing: revenue and margin recovery is repeatedly placed in H2 and FY28. It was defensive on EBITDA-to-PBT comparability and on the 10% PBT target, and evasive on tax write-backs and on Kolkata land monetisation timing.
